summary: Mount Terrill on the Fishlake Plateau is listed only as an unknown or undocumented site; no lookout is confirmed, and a nearby guard station shares its name.

facts.status_note: Listed only as an unknown or undocumented site; no lookout is confirmed here.

access.note: In the Fishlake National Forest; a climbing guide says no permit is needed unless you cut firewood.

visit.trail_note: A worn trail leads to the summit from nearby UM Pass.

evidence.supports: small, rounded peak north of Seven Mile Valley on the Fishlake Plateau; also called White Knob
evidence.quote: Mount Terrill - also known as White Knob - is a small, rounded peak north of Seven Mile Valley high on the Fishlake Plateau.

evidence.supports: few visitors, mostly ATV riders; worn trail from UM Pass
evidence.quote: The mountain sees few visitors, mostly ATVers, as a worn trail leads to the summit from nearby UM Pass.

evidence.supports: in the Fishlake National Forest; no permit needed unless cutting firewood
evidence.quote: Mount Terrill is located in Fishlake National Forest. No permits are necessary unless you want to cut firewood.

evidence.supports: Mount Terrel in Sevier County is on the Forest Fire Lookout Association's Utah list of unknown or undocumented sites
the list is of unknown or undocumented sites
such a site moves to the lookout list only if evidence shows regular fire-lookout use
evidence.quote: If evidence or documentation is uncovered showing that any of these were actually used as regular wildland fire lookout sites, they will be moved to the lookout lists.

evidence.supports: the name is listed among sites the author has not visited
the name appears on WillhiteWeb's list as Mount Terrel

'Nothing known' about a lookout; the entry calls Mt. Terrill in Sevier County the probable match, with good views over timber in the Fish Lake National Forest (the author's inference, not a documented lookout)
evidence.quote: Nothing known. But seems straightforward that there is a Mt. Terrill in Sevier County with good views over lots of timber in the Fish Lake National Forest, just north of Fish Lake.

evidence.supports: the Mt Terrill Guard Station is in the Fishlake National Forest
evidence.quote: Mt Terrill Guard Station is located on the Fishlake National Forest in Central Utah about 30 miles southeast of Salina.

evidence.supports: the guard station is a two-room cabin, near the top of the Seven Mile-Gooseberry road
evidence.quote: The rustic Mt. Terrill Guard Station is a two room cabin with a kitchen and bedroom.

evidence.supports: the cabin sits near the top of the paved Seven Mile-Gooseberry road
evidence.quote: The cabin sits at near the top of the paved Seven Mile-Gooseberry road #640 between Salina and Fish Lake.

corrections.why: The climbing guide and WillhiteWeb's own text spell the peak Mount Terrill. The record's Terrel is the spelling in the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and WillhiteWeb's list.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Terrel (the Forest Fire Lookout Association list and WillhiteWeb's list) and Terrill (the climbing guide and WillhiteWeb's text) appear to name the same Sevier County peak. The story uses Terrill.

sources.title: Mount Terrill : Climbing, Hiking & Mountaineering : SummitPost

notes_for_editor: No source read describes a fire lookout on Mount Terrill. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as unknown or undocumented. WillhiteWeb lists it among sites its author has not visited, says 'Nothing known', and points to Mount Terrill as the likely site; that is a guess, not a documented lookout. The Mt Terrill Guard Station is a cabin, not a tower, and may be the source of confusion. Name correction (Terrel to Terrill) is proposed for a human to review. Consider marking the record unconfirmed or hidden.
